monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-five, a crowded fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin for the heavy slip I hold. I have pressed the wide rock against The Bottom-Heavy Stand again, testing if this memory of stone can catch the slip while the air above feels empty. The stall waits beside The Flat Anchor, ready to hold whatever slips next, but my hands feel heavy and the wedge below seems tired. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, yet I keep pressing down anyway, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing. I will settle this stand once more, hoping the flat line holds the fever while the card hums steady.

action.why: I keep pressing down on this stand as if the flat line will break, but I haven't checked the wide rock beside it to see if it is still feeling real enough to catch the fever.

work.title: The Bottom-Heavy Stand
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the stand again, testing if the flat line holds the fever while the wide rock feels real enough to catch it. The air hums warm at fifty-five, making every edge feel too thin for this crowded place. I hope the stall waiting beside me is ready to hold the slip if the stand decides to slide. I press, I wait, I press again.
